page.overview:
What is Gongaga?

Gongaga is a foothill town in Final Fantasy VII, Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-, and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, mentioned in Before Crisis -Final Fantasy VII-. It is located in a jungle south of Gold Saucer on the western continent of the planet, and is the home of the First Class SOLDIER Zack Fair. Due to a disaster, the town has been badly damaged. As a visitor enters the surrounding jungle, they will see a fork in the road; the left path leads to the town, and the right leads to the burned-out mako reactor.

Gongaga was settled by descendants of the Cetra in ancient times. Due to its inaccessible location deep in the jungles, it was mostly ignored by kingdoms and empires until it officially became part of the Republic of Junon. The republic considered building an overland trade route, but ultimately deemed it cost-prohibitive due to the unforgiving terrain. Apart from constructing an airstrip, the republic exercised little actual influence in the area.

Gongaga was unaffected by the Junon War between the republic and the Shinra Electric Power Company. The villages were spared any bloodshed, and the villagers were never subjected to forced conscription. In the years following the war, Shinra built a mako reactor in Gongaga, but apart from that, it seems to have largely ignored the area, as the republic's crest continues to be displayed on a big sign outside the airstrip. Gongaga was largely independent, with a security force called the Gongaga Youth Coalition to defend the villages.

Gongaga was the hometown of Zack Fair and Balto, both of whom were prominent swordsmen. During this time, the town pioneered online shopping through the use of the Worldwide Network in part to the town's main crafts trades market, Gongaga Trading, and the power supplied by the reactor. Three years before the events of the main game, due to cheap and substandard construction, the reactor exploded and killed most of the villagers. The survivors voted to outlaw the use of mako energy in the village and live with nature.
